I don’t have a built‑in tool that talks straight to VirusTotal’s API, so I can’t pull live data for you right now. What I *can* do is walk you through exactly what you’d send to VirusTotal (or write a quick script) and then sketch out what the JSON reply will look like—so you’ll know whether your own query worked when you run it yourself. --- ### 1️⃣ What URL & headers does VirusTotal expect? | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/records` *(new v3)*
OR
`https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain-reputation//dns_report` *(old v2 – still works for many users)* | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Headers** | ```text\nX-AUTH-API-Key: \nAccept: application/json\n``` | For the domain “yahoo.com” replace `` accordingly: ``` https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain-reputation/yahoo.com/dns_report ``` If you’re using the newer `/api/v3/...` style, the path would be something like: ``` https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/risk ``` (See the official docs for exact endpoints.) --- ### 2️⃣ Quick cURL Example ```bash curl -s \ --request GET \ --url https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain-reputation/yahoo.com/dns_report \ --header "x-apikey: api_key123" ``` Replace `api_key123` with your actual key. --- ### 3️⃣ Sample Response Structure Below is a *typical* snippet you might see back from VirusTotal. It isn’t the real answer for Yahoo at this moment—it just shows the fields you’ll encounter. ```json { "data": { "id": "yahoo.com", "attributes": { "last_analysis_date": 1715900000, "last_dns_query_time": 1715899999, "resolutions": [ { "ip_address": "98.137.246.7", "record_type": "A", "ttl": 300, "first_seen": 1609459200, "last_seen": 1700459200 }, { "ipv6_address": "2600:1408::b5d:ff00", "record_type": "AAAA", "ttl": 600, "first_seen": 1612137600, "last_seen": 1703457600 } ], "mx_records": [ {"exchange":"mta-a.mail.yahoo.com","priority":10} ] } } } ``` Key points: | Field | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `resolutions[]` | List of A/AAAA records seen over time | | `mx_records[]` | Mail exchange servers | | `first_seen`, `last_seen` | When each record first/most recently appeared | | `ttl` | Time‑to‑live value reported by authoritative nameservers | --- ### 4️⃣ How to interpret the result 1. **Count the entries** – If there are multiple IP addresses under `"resolutions"` you’ve got load balancing or CDN in play. 2. **Check TTL values** – Shorter TTL means more frequent updates. 3. **Look at dates** – Compare `first_seen` vs. `last_seen`; a long gap may indicate stale data. --- ### 5️⃣ Common pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Double‑check the API key spelling and ensure it has permission for the “Domain Reputation” scope. | | **Rate limit exceeded** | Wait ~60 seconds before retrying or upgrade plan. | | **Empty `resolutions` array** | Some domains hide their DNS info behind privacy services; try querying via another resolver or wait until they publish publicly. | --- #### TL;DR Run the above curl (or equivalent HTTP client code), pass your key (`api_key123`) in the `x-apikey` header, hit the `/v2/domain-reputation/{domain}/dns_report` endpoint, and parse the returned JSON. That gives you all known DNS records that VirusTotal has observed for `yahoo.com`.
